resources.string: Blocks touches from a damaged part of the screen and gives you a trackpad and an on-screen cursor to drive the phone with instead.

The bubble follows your finger and the cursor moves with it. Let go and the bubble slides back to its spot, while the cursor stays where you left it, so you can cross the screen in several strokes. The bubble shows the time. Triple tap it to switch it off: it disappears completely, along with the cursor, so edge swipes and everything behind it work normally. Press volume up and down together to bring it back, or to switch it off without reaching for it. It also lifts itself above the keyboard while one is open.
Block touches in the damaged area
The outline and the label are drawn only while this screen is open, so nothing marks the screen while you use the phone. Touches are blocked either way.

Slide to move the cursor — lifting your finger does not tap.
Tap without sliding to click where the cursor is.
Double tap and release to long press.
Double tap and, without lifting, slide to drag: slide straight away to scroll, or rest a moment first to pick something up.
Triple tap the bubble to switch it off; volume up + down together switches it off or back on.
Slide to move · tap to click · double tap to hold
Drag the bubble where you want it and let go.
Hidden. Volume up + down together brings it back.
The bubble will come back here from now on.

Touches in the damaged area are blocked.

Lets Mouse tap, long press and drag where you put the on-screen cursor, and use Back, Home and Recents from the floating trackpad. It also looks at where the keyboard is, so the trackpad can move out of its way, and listens for volume up and down together as a shortcut. Mouse does not read the text or contents of your screen.
